subject: Hosted API: custody, retention & erasure Q&A (Greenline Health)

Subject: Hosted API security questionnaire (data residency/retention)

Hi Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our compliance team has a short questionnaire focused on where data lives and how it is retained/erased when using Redwood's hosted API. I attached Greenline_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf — the relevant sections are Q12–Q18 (data residency, retention, deletion).

High-level asks:
1) Where customer input and derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes) reside (region/accounting).
2) Default retention windows for generation request logs, embeddings, telemetry, and backups.
3) How erasure requests are executed (time to completion, evidence).
4) Any cross‑border transfers or subprocessors we should be aware of.

Can you provide a concise response pack (bullet answers + any evidence links) our auditors can consume? We need this by EOW (Friday).

Appreciate it — Evan

Evan —

Thanks for sending this over. Forwarding our initial answers and looping in Ben (Security) and Priyom (Solutions) for any operational details and evidence links. I've attached a short summary (GI_Responses_Summary.docx) with the items below.

Core responses (hosted API):

1) Data residency & storage - Customer request payloads, temporary inference state (KV cache), and derived artifacts (embeddings stored when customer chooses to persist them) are stored in region-specific tenant buckets based on account configuration. Default region is us-west-2 for US accounts unless a different region is requested during onboarding.

2) Retention windows - Default retention for:
  • Request logs (metadata only, no raw prompt by default): 30 days.
  • Full request payloads (if customer enables request logging): retained only per customer configuration; default 0 days unless opted-in.
  • Embeddings and persistable artifacts: persist until customer deletes them or the tenant is deprovisioned; snapshot backups retained for 90 days by default.
  • Telemetry & operational metrics (aggregated): 24 months for service performance analysis, never tied to tenant identifiers in dashboards.
  • Backup snapshots (service-level): encrypted snapshots retained 90 days, rolled per snapshot policy.

3) Deletion & erasure process - Three paths:
  A) Tenant-initiated via Console/API: a tenant admin can request a full data purge. This triggers (i) immediate soft-delete mark in the control plane, (ii) queued background purge jobs that scrub data from active stores and cache, and (iii) deletion from snapshot rotation windows at next snapshot expiry. Typical completion: 24–72 hours depending on dataset size and region.
  B) On-demand legal/DSR requests: we accept formal erasure requests via support with authenticated account proof. We produce an erasure report (job id + timestamps + affected object ids) once complete.
  C) Temporary caches: KV/prefix caches are ephemeral by design and evicted per LRU/TTL within minutes to hours; we actively purge tenant-scoped KV caches when a purge request is issued.

4) Evidence & auditability - After purge completion we provide a deletion report containing: job id, start/end timestamps, list of object identifiers removed, and the S3 object deletion markers where applicable. Audit logs for control-plane operations (who requested purge, job status changes) are retained for 12 months. We can share example redacted reports on request.

5) Cross‑border transfers and subprocessors - Hosts and storage reside in the customer-chosen region. For US accounts we do not transfer customer storage outside the US except for ephemeral processing in a compatible region for autoscaling events. Subprocessors (cloud provider, managed DB, monitoring vendors) are listed in our SOC pack; we will supply an up-to-date vendor list to your procurement team.

6) Encryption & access controls - Data at rest: AES-256. In transit: TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3. Tenant keys may be managed via Customer-Managed KMS for Private/Dedicated customers; for hosted accounts we support bring-your-own‑KMS on request via an enterprise contract for region-specific keys. Role-based access controls and least-privilege IAM policies restrict access to stored objects; human access is recorded in audit logs.

7) Backups & disaster recovery - Snapshots are encrypted and stored in region; cross-region replication only enabled for accounts that opt into multi-region DR. Snapshots are subject to the 90-day retention noted above and are included in purge operations when a tenant requests full data deletion.

Attachments: GI_Responses_Summary.docx

Monica / Evan — quick technical clarifications and an attached snippet from our erase playbook. Highlights:

• Control-plane audit logs: retained 12 months by default; operational logs for debug are 90 days unless customer opts into extended retention. We can export logs to a customer-owned S3 bucket for longer retention on request (contracted feature).

• Erasure timing: for small tenants completion is typically <24 hours; for large datasets (>100M objects) jobs run in parallel, and final artifact deletion from immutable snapshots can take up to the next snapshot purge cycle (<=90 days). We mark snapshots for expedited rotation when given an explicit full-tenant deletion request.

• KV cache behavior: cache entries are not persisted to long-term storage; they are tenant-scoped in memory/pinned nodes and are zeroed and invalidated when a purge request runs. We do not rely on cache TTLs alone for compliance — purge jobs explicitly sweep cache indexes.

• Evidence delivery: we will produce a deletion_report.zip containing a small JSON manifest (object ids removed) and a signed control-plane log excerpt. We can upload that package to a secure Drive link or push into your procurement tracker (HubSpot).

I've attached erase_playbook_snippet.txt with the job id format example and an example redacted manifest.

Ben Carter
